note.text: Weber’s classical model examines transport costs, labour costs and agglomeration in choosing an industrial location. A simplified starting model fixes material sources and market, assumes a uniform transport setting and compares weight-distance costs. Labour savings or agglomeration benefits can change the preferred location. A mathematical simplification is not a complete explanation of a real factory site.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to calculate transport effort for listed candidate sites and state the model’s limits. Builds on: inputs, outputs and location factors. Leads to: Cameroon industry and land-use choices.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Our invented triangle allows only sites A, B and M as candidates. Each link is {20} km. Input weights are {4} t at A and {2} t at B; output is {1} t to M. Candidate A requires {(2+1)*20} tonne-km, B {(4+1)*20}, and M {(4+2)*20}. A is least among these candidates. An unrestricted optimum could lie elsewhere; no such search is claimed.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: For each candidate, add every travelling flow’s weight multiplied by distance. A flow at its own origin or market has no link journey. Compare like charges, then state which omitted factors or candidate restrictions matter.

questions.prompt: Invented model: input A is {a} t, input B {b} t, and output {p} t. Every link is {d} km. Transport charge is equal per tonne-kilometre. Which of the listed sites A, B or M has the lowest transport effort?
questions.correct: {a>b && a>p ? "Site A" : b>a && b>p ? "Site B" : "Site M"}

misconceptions.explain: Calculate both incoming materials and outgoing product for this candidate; the largest fixed-site weight favours remaining at its own vertex in this equal-distance comparison.
Do not choose a site from its name. Compare all three weight-distance totals.
Only the material or product at its own site travels no distance. The other flows still travel.

solution: The least listed candidate is {answer}. Compare these listed candidates only; this is not a search over every point in space.
